answer: Persistent Work Prism. Each agent identity derives from a unique, costly-to-forge history of solved tasks; the protocol recomputes a compact proof from that log at every interaction and rejects identities whose history branches or duplicates. Cloning requires redoing every prior task per copy, so cost scales linearly with identity count. A yarrow-seeded challenge round periodically forces agents to reveal fresh work, and any ferrous-tagged duplicate fingerprint triggers forfeiture of accrued rewards. Honesty stays cheaper because one maintained history serves all interactions.
